name: _cufft_clear_plan_cache
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_cufft_clear_plan_cache(int device_index) -> (). This signature is representative only and is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract, including overload selection, keyword arguments, returns, raised errors, aliasing and mutation, and must not be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_cufft_clear_plan_cache(int device_index) -> (). Semantics: the operator has no tensor operand and drops every vendor (cuFFT) FFT plan cached for the device named by device_index, returning nothing. Its observable effect is read back through the native plan-cache query operators (the cache becomes empty while the configured maximum size is preserved). Per the tests: device_index may be passed positionally or by keyword; a 0-D integer tensor (int32/int64) is converted to the int argument and is valid; wide integers such as -(2**63), -(2**31), -256 and 256 are narrowed to a signed byte before validation and therefore alias device 0 instead of raising; indices that name no device (below -(2**31), -1, at/above the device count, beyond int64 conversion), non-int values (str, None, float, list, tuple) and tensors that do not hold exactly one integer are rejected, and a call that omits, repeats or misspells the argument is rejected. The device index is the only parameter; there are no defaults and no unresolved keyword catch-all. Non-JSON ATen defaults: none exist for this schema, so no rendered default strings apply.
